ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the bracket is fixed on the horizontal ground, and its inclined smooth straight rod makes an angle of 30° with the ground. Two rings A and B are threaded on the straight rod and are connected by a light rope passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The size of the pulley is negligible, and the entire device is in the same vertical plane. When the rings are in equilibrium, rope OA is vertical, and the angle between rope OB and the straight rod is 30°. Then the ratio of the masses of rings A and B is (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an inclined smooth straight rod fixed on the horizontal ground, and the angle between the straight rod and the horizontal ground is marked as 30°. Rings A and B are both sleeved on this inclined rod; above there is a smooth fixed pulley O, and a light rope passes over the pulley. One end goes vertically downward from the pulley and is connected to A, that is, OA is vertical, and the other end is connected obliquely downward to B; in the figure, the condition for the angle between OB and the inclined rod is 30°. The entire structure is in the same vertical plane. Reasoning: Let the tension in the rope be T. The rod is smooth, so the supporting force exerted by the rod on each ring is perpendicular to the rod; it is enough to write equilibrium along the direction of the rod. For ring A: OA is vertical, and the component of the vertical tension T upward along the inclined rod is T sin30°; the component of gravity m_A g downward along the inclined rod is m_A g sin30°. Equilibrium gives T sin30° = m_A g sin30°, so T = m_A g. For ring B: the angle between OB and the inclined rod is 30°, and the component of the tension upward along the inclined rod is T cos30°; the component of gravity m_B g downward along the inclined rod is m_B g sin30°. Equilibrium gives T cos30° = m_B g sin30°. Substituting T = m_A g gives m_A g cos30° = m_B g sin30°, so m_A/m_B = sin30°/cos30° = tan30° = 1/√3. Therefore m_A:m_B = 1:√3.
